questions.cardText:
[Ecology] In ecology, what are “biomes”?
A. Microscopic organisms in water
B. Genetic variations within a species
C. Large naturally occurring communities of flora and fauna
Answer: C.
questions.en: In ecology, what is the term for a large, naturally occurring community of flora and fauna shaped by a region’s climate, such as tundra or tropical rainforest?
questions.de: Wie heißt in der Ökologie eine große, natürlich vorkommende Lebensgemeinschaft aus Flora und Fauna, die vom Klima einer Region geprägt ist, etwa Tundra oder tropischer Regenwald?

timeline.labelEn: International Biological Program, whose projects popularised the concept of the biome
timeline.labelDe: Internationales Biologisches Programm, dessen Projekte den Begriff des Bioms populär machten

questions.notes: Card's definition question reversed into asking for the term.

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] What Japanese writing system would be used to write the word “konnichiwa”?
A. Hiragana  B. Katakana  C. Kanji
Answer: A. Japanese uses three distinct writing systems: Hiragana is mostly used for native Japanese words and grammatical functions (e.g., こんにちは or konnichiwa for “hello”), Katakana for foreign words and names (e.g., バナナ or banana for “banana”), and Kanji for nouns, verbs, and adjectives (e.g., 山 or yama for “mountain”).
questions.en: In which Japanese script is the greeting “konnichiwa” (hello) usually written?
questions.de: In welcher japanischen Schrift wird der Gruß „konnichiwa“ (Hallo) üblicherweise geschrieben?

timeline.labelEn: Hiragana is standardised to one character per syllable
timeline.labelDe: Die Hiragana werden auf ein Zeichen pro Silbe vereinheitlicht

questions.notes: Usually spelled こんにちは in hiragana; it can also be written with kanji as 今日は, so 'usually' is needed.
